questions.stem: What does „die Klimaneutralität“ mean?
options: A neutral position in political debates on climate
A tax charged on every product that harms the climate
Climate neutrality, with no net greenhouse gas emissions
A climate with neither very hot nor very cold weather
questions.explanation: A „klimaneutral“ company or country balances any emissions it still produces, so its net effect on the climate is zero. „Neutral“ here refers to emissions, not to weather or opinions.

questions.stem: What does „der Atomausstieg“ mean?
options: A leak from a nuclear power station
The export of nuclear waste
The phasing out of nuclear power
The building of new nuclear plants
questions.explanation: „Aussteigen“ is to get out, so „der Ausstieg“ is an exit: „der Atomausstieg“ is the decision to stop generating nuclear power. „Der Kohleausstieg“ is the same idea for coal.

questions.stem: What is „die Kreislaufwirtschaft“?
options: An economy that depends on tourists travelling in circles
A regional economy based on local farmers' markets
A system of trade between neighbouring countries
A circular economy that reuses and recycles materials
questions.explanation: „Der Kreislauf“ is a cycle, so products and materials are kept in use rather than thrown away. It is the opposite of „die Wegwerfgesellschaft“, the throwaway society.

questions.stem: What is „das Pfand“ on a drink bottle?
options: A tax on drinks that pays for cleaning up the streets and parks
A fine for throwing a bottle away in a public place
A discount given for buying drinks by the crate
A deposit that is refunded when the bottle is returned
questions.explanation: The deposit is paid at the till and given back when the empty bottle is taken to a return point, which keeps bottles out of the rubbish. It is a refund, so it is not a tax or a fine.

questions.stem: What does „die Wegwerfgesellschaft“ mean?
options: The recycling industry
The rubbish collection
The waste tax
The throwaway society
questions.explanation: „Wegwerfen“ is to throw away, so the compound criticises a society that discards things instead of repairing or reusing them.

questions.stem: What does „die Artenvielfalt“ mean?
options: A range of products
Biodiversity
Cultural diversity
A variety show
questions.explanation: „Die Art“ here is a species and „die Vielfalt“ is variety, so „die Artenvielfalt“ is the variety of species in an area. Cultural diversity is „die kulturelle Vielfalt“.

questions.stem: What is „der Treibhauseffekt“?
options: The greenhouse effect
The hothouse flower
The fuel shortage
The driving force
questions.explanation: „Das Treibhaus“ is a greenhouse, so „der Treibhauseffekt“ is the warming caused by gases that trap heat. The gases themselves are „Treibhausgase“.

questions.stem: Which group lists only renewable sources of energy?
options: Atomkraft, Sonnenenergie und Erdöl
Windkraft, Sonnenenergie und Wasserkraft
Windkraft, Erdgas und Sonnenenergie
Kohle, Wasserkraft, Windkraft und Sonnenenergie
questions.explanation: Wind, solar and hydro power are all renewable. „Erdgas“ (natural gas), „Kohle“ (coal) and „Erdöl“ (oil) are fossil fuels, and „Atomkraft“ is nuclear power, which is not counted as renewable.

questions.stem: What does „Wir müssen die Ressourcen der Erde schonen“ mean?
options: We must share the Earth's resources
We must spend the Earth's resources
We must measure the Earth's resources
We must conserve the Earth's resources
questions.explanation: „Schonen“ is to spare or treat carefully. It is a useful verb for persuasive writing on the environment, alongside „schützen“ (to protect).

questions.stem: What does „Der Meeresspiegel steigt, weil das Eis an den Polen schmilzt“ mean?
options: The ice at the poles is melting because the sea level is rising
The sea level is falling because the ice at the poles is freezing
The sea level is rising because the ice at the poles is melting
The level of lakes is rising because the ice at the poles is melting
questions.explanation: „Der Meeresspiegel“ is sea level, and „weil“ introduces the cause: the melting. Reversing cause and effect is the trap, and „der See“ (lake) is not „das Meer“.

questions.stem: „Elektroautos gelten als umweltfreundlich. Kritiker geben jedoch zu bedenken, dass für die Batterien seltene Rohstoffe abgebaut werden müssen.“ What do the critics point out?
options: Making the batteries requires mining scarce raw materials
Electric cars produce more exhaust than petrol cars do
The batteries are too expensive for most drivers to buy
Electric cars cannot be recharged from renewable energy
questions.explanation: „Zu bedenken geben“ is to point out a concern, and „Rohstoffe abbauen“ is to mine raw materials. „Gelten als“ (are considered) signals that the first claim is about to be questioned.

questions.stem: „Die Forschung an erneuerbaren Energien wird stark gefördert, damit das Land unabhängiger von importierten Brennstoffen wird.“ What does the sentence say?
options: Research is being cut back because imported fuels are now much cheaper
Research is paid for by the companies that import the fuels
Research shows that imported fuels are better for the climate
Research is funded so the country relies less on imported fuels
questions.explanation: „Fördern“ here means to fund or support, and „damit“ gives the purpose: more independence. „Fördern“ is also used for mining coal, but with „Forschung“ it can only mean support.

questions.stem: What does the slogan „Global denken, lokal handeln“ mean?
options: Trade globally, buy locally
Think locally, act globally
Travel globally, live locally
Think globally, act locally
questions.explanation: „Denken“ is to think and „handeln“ is to act. „Handeln“ can also mean to trade, which is the trap, but in this slogan it means taking action.

questions.stem: What is „der Fachkräftemangel“?
options: A shortage of skilled workers
A lack of specialist subjects at school
An oversupply of university graduates
A shortage of jobs for young people
questions.explanation: „Die Fachkraft“ is a skilled worker and „der Mangel“ a shortage. It is often linked to arguments for immigration and vocational training.

questions.stem: „In dem kleinen Ort leben nur wenige hundert Menschen, doch an manchen Tagen kommen Tausende Tagesgäste. Viele Einheimische fühlen sich wie Statisten in einem Freilichtmuseum.“ How do many locals feel?
options: Pleased that the visitors have given the town new life
Proud to work as guides in the town's open-air museum
Worried that too few visitors come to the town
As if their town had become a stage set for visitors
questions.explanation: „Statisten“ are film extras and „ein Freilichtmuseum“ is an open-air museum: the locals feel like background figures in their own town. „Doch“ sets the small population against the crowds.

questions.stem: What does „die Flugscham“ describe?
options: Annoyance at delays and cancelled flights
Pride at having flown to many distant countries
Guilt about flying because of its effect on the climate
Fear of flying that stops people from ever boarding a plane
questions.explanation: „Die Scham“ is shame, so „die Flugscham“ is feeling bad about the emissions from flying. Fear of flying is „die Flugangst“, a different compound.

questions.stem: What is „die Barrierefreiheit“?
options: The right to enter any public building free of charge
Access for people with disabilities, without obstacles
The removal of border controls between countries
Freedom from tariffs and other barriers to trade
questions.explanation: A „barrierefrei“ building, website or bus can be used by everyone, including wheelchair users and people with impaired sight. It is a key term when writing about diversity and inclusion.

questions.stem: What does „den CO₂-Ausstoß senken“ mean?
options: To tax CO₂ emissions
To trade CO₂ emissions
To reduce CO₂ emissions
To measure CO₂ emissions
questions.explanation: „Der Ausstoß“ is output or emission and „senken“ is to lower. It is standard phrasing in any text on climate policy.

questions.stem: What does „die Fremdenfeindlichkeit“ mean?
options: Xenophobia
Homesickness
Hospitality
Tourism
questions.explanation: „Fremd“ is foreign or strange and „feindlich“ is hostile, so the compound is hostility towards foreigners. Its opposite in spirit is „die Gastfreundschaft“, hospitality.

questions.stem: What does „Begegnungen mit anderen Kulturen helfen, Vorurteile abzubauen“ mean?
options: Meeting other cultures helps people to make judgements faster
Meeting other cultures tends to build up new prejudices
Meeting other cultures helps people to agree on laws
Meeting other cultures helps to break down prejudices
questions.explanation: „Das Vorurteil“ is a prejudice and „abbauen“ is to reduce or dismantle. Reading „abbauen“ as 'build up' reverses it; that would be „aufbauen“.

questions.stem: What is „die Willkommenskultur“?
options: A government office that issues visitor visas
A festival held to welcome the start of spring
An attitude of welcoming and supporting newcomers
The custom of greeting guests at the front door
questions.explanation: „Die Willkommenskultur“ describes openness towards migrants and refugees, from the state and from ordinary citizens. The term is central to the German debate on migration.

questions.stem: „Integration ist keine Einbahnstraße: Sie verlangt Offenheit von denen, die kommen, und von denen, die schon da sind.“ What does the writer argue?
options: Integration is mainly the task of the new arrivals in the community
Integration fails whenever newcomers hold on to their own culture and language
Integration happens quickly once newcomers have found a job
Integration needs openness from newcomers and from those already living there
questions.explanation: „Keine Einbahnstraße“ (not a one-way street) says the effort must go both ways, and the two „denen, die …“ clauses name both groups. Placing the burden only on newcomers is the view the writer rejects.

questions.stem: What does „die Meinungsfreiheit“ mean?
options: Freedom of movement
Freedom of the press
Freedom of expression
Freedom of religion
questions.explanation: „Die Meinung“ is an opinion, so „die Meinungsfreiheit“ is the right to say what you think. Freedom of the press is „die Pressefreiheit“, a related but separate right.

questions.stem: What does „Quellen kritisch hinterfragen“ mean?
options: To criticise sources in public
To ask sources for an interview
To look for the source of a river
To question sources critically
questions.explanation: „Die Quelle“ is a source (also a spring) and „hinterfragen“ is to question what lies behind something. It is the core skill in the media literacy debate.

questions.stem: What is „die Pressefreiheit“?
options: Free newspapers
A press release
A free pass for journalists
Freedom of the press
questions.explanation: „Die Presse“ is the press and „die Freiheit“ is freedom. A press release is „eine Pressemitteilung“.

questions.stem: What is „die Filterblase“?
options: A software setting in the browser that blocks unwanted advertising
A water filter sold through online advertising
A message that is deleted once it has been read
A filter bubble, where users mostly see views like their own
questions.explanation: Algorithms show users more of what they already like, so they end up in a bubble of similar opinions. An ad blocker is „ein Werbeblocker“.

questions.stem: What is „Schleichwerbung“?
options: Advertising that appears in the cinema before a film
Advertising that is sent by post to every household in a town
Advertising that is banned because it is dishonest
Advertising hidden in content without being labelled as an ad
questions.explanation: „Schleichen“ is to creep, so „Schleichwerbung“ creeps in unannounced, for example an influencer showing a product without saying it is paid. It is criticised for being covert, not for appearing in a particular place.

questions.stem: What is „die Zielgruppe“ of an advertisement?
options: The winning team
The target audience
The sales target
The final goal
questions.explanation: „Das Ziel“ is a target or goal and „die Gruppe“ a group, so „die Zielgruppe“ is the audience an advertisement is aimed at. Identifying it is part of analysing a text's purpose and audience.

questions.stem: „Neun von zehn Zahnärzten empfehlen unsere Zahnpasta.“ Which advertising technique is used?
options: An emotional appeal to the reader's family
An appeal to expert authority backed by a statistic
Creating urgency with a limited-time offer
A celebrity endorsement from a famous athlete
questions.explanation: Dentists are presented as experts, and „neun von zehn“ makes the claim look measured. No deadline, celebrity or family is involved.

questions.stem: „Soziale Medien verbinden Menschen weltweit. Gleichzeitig fühlen sich viele Jugendliche einsamer denn je, weil sie sich ständig mit anderen vergleichen.“ What is the writer's point?
options: Young people feel lonely mainly because they cannot use social media often enough
Social media mainly connects older people rather than young people
Social media connects people, yet comparison leaves many young people lonelier
Social media makes young people less lonely because they can compare notes
questions.explanation: „Gleichzeitig“ (at the same time) introduces a paradox, and „weil sie sich ständig vergleichen“ gives the cause of the loneliness. „Einsamer denn je“ means lonelier than ever.

questions.stem: „Werbung für ungesunde Lebensmittel sollte in Kinderprogrammen verboten werden, denn Kinder können Werbung oft nicht von Inhalten unterscheiden.“ What is the reason given?
options: Unhealthy food is more expensive than healthy food
Advertisers already avoid placing ads in children's programs
Children often cannot tell advertising apart from content
Children watch far too much television in the afternoon
questions.explanation: „Denn“ introduces the reason, and „von etwas unterscheiden“ is to tell apart. The argument rests on children's vulnerability, not on cost or viewing time.

questions.stem: What is „die Reizüberflutung“?
options: A sudden loss of the internet connection at home
Overload from a constant stream of information and stimuli
A flood warning sent to every phone in a region
The excitement felt before a big event or trip
questions.explanation: „Der Reiz“ is a stimulus and „die Überflutung“ a flood, so the word describes being swamped by notifications, screens and noise. It is a common term in debates about digital media and wellbeing.

questions.stem: „Lernprogramme mit künstlicher Intelligenz passen sich dem Tempo jedes Schülers an. Lehrkräfte ersetzen können sie aber nicht.“ What does the writer claim?
options: AI programs adapt to each student but cannot replace teachers
AI programs will soon replace teachers in most schools
AI programs work at one fixed speed for every student
Teachers adapt AI programs to suit their own teaching pace
questions.explanation: „Sich anpassen an“ is to adapt to, and „aber“ introduces the limit. The word order „Lehrkräfte ersetzen können sie nicht“ fronts the object for emphasis: replacing teachers is what they cannot do.

questions.stem: „Manche Firmen schalten nach Feierabend ihre E-Mail-Server ab, damit die Mitarbeiter nicht ständig erreichbar sein müssen.“ What is the aim?
options: That the firms can save money on their electricity
That staff finish their work before going home
That emails are checked by managers overnight
That staff do not have to be contactable all the time
questions.explanation: „Damit“ introduces the purpose, and „erreichbar sein“ is to be reachable. The measure protects free time after work, a key issue in the impact of technology on work.

questions.stem: What does „die Überwachung“ mean?
options: Surveillance
Supervision of homework
A wake-up call
An overview
questions.explanation: „Überwachen“ is to monitor, so „die Überwachung“ is surveillance, as in „Videoüberwachung“. „Der Überblick“ is an overview.

questions.stem: „Einerseits erleichtert KI viele Aufgaben, andererseits wirft sie Fragen zum Datenschutz auf.“ What does the sentence do?
options: It claims that AI has already solved most privacy problems
It says AI makes tasks harder but keeps personal data safe
It weighs a benefit of AI against a concern about privacy
It argues that AI should be banned to protect personal data
questions.explanation: „Einerseits … andererseits“ (on the one hand … on the other) sets two sides against each other, the core move of evaluative writing. „Fragen aufwerfen“ is to raise questions; no conclusion is drawn.

questions.stem: Who invented the paper coffee filter, registered in Dresden in 1908?
options: Clara Schumann
Melitta Bentz
Margarete Steiff
Bertha Benz
questions.explanation: Melitta Bentz's invention founded a company that still bears her name. Margarete Steiff made soft toys, and Bertha Benz made the first long-distance drive in a motor car.

questions.stem: Why are X-rays called „Röntgenstrahlen“ in German?
options: After the small town of Röntgen, where they were first used in hospitals
Because „Röntgen“ is the German word for bone
After the company that built the first scanner
After Wilhelm Conrad Röntgen, who discovered them in 1895
questions.explanation: German names the rays after the physicist, and „röntgen“ is even a verb, to X-ray. Röntgen received the first Nobel Prize in Physics for the discovery.

questions.stem: What does „die Hassrede im Netz“ refer to?
options: Arguments between friends online
Speeches broadcast over the internet
Online reviews with low ratings
Hate speech on the internet
questions.explanation: „Der Hass“ is hatred and „das Netz“ is the internet. The term comes up in discussions of free speech and the responsibility of platforms.

questions.stem: „Der technische Fortschritt ist nicht aufzuhalten, aber wir entscheiden, wie wir ihn nutzen.“ What does the writer suggest?
options: Progress cannot be stopped, but people choose how to use it
Progress can still be stopped if enough people decide to stop using it
Progress has stopped because people no longer use it well
Progress cannot be used until people decide to accept it
questions.explanation: „Nicht aufzuhalten“ (sein + zu + infinitive) means cannot be stopped. „Aber“ then returns responsibility to people, so the writer accepts progress while stressing choice.
